identity.purpose: Illustrate a prescribed fragment release and cloud stretching over the first three revolutions.

physics.model: Edition-owned elliptic Kepler propagation from Cartesian release states, evaluated directly at every displayed time.
physics.incomingGeometry: Two equal-weight circular bodies meet at [R+h,0,0]; velocity inclinations +55 and -35 degrees give perpendicular paths.
physics.sampleWeights: Equal representative weights, not physical masses or predicted fragment yield.
physics.randomAlgorithm: Mulberry32; uniform spherical direction from uniform z and azimuth; magnitude = cube root of a third uniform variate. Paired opposite vectors fill a ball uniformly in velocity space.

releaseSpeedMPerSecond.distribution: Uniform volume in the velocity ball, from zero to the selected maximum speed. Same relative magnitudes and directions on replay; no fitted breakup distribution.

physics.momentum: Equal-weight family means conserve total incoming linear momentum; paired kicks sum to zero.
physics.energy: Relative mean velocity contraction removes more kinetic energy than the kicks add throughout the allowed slider range.
physics.frame: Synthetic inertial Cartesian axes mapped to Three world (x,z,-y). Earth rotates about its polar axis at 7.292115e-5 rad/s, with arbitrary orientation at contact and no dated geographical claim.
physics.drawnEarth: Existing WGS84 ellipsoid and pinned Natural Earth geography. Experiment heights are above the spherical reference, distinct from WGS84 geodetic altitude.
excluded: NASA Standard Breakup Model or fitted size/mass/velocity distributions
Atmospheric drag, reentry and long-term decay
Oblateness / J2, third bodies and radiation pressure

presentation.label: AN INDICATIVE SIMULATION
presentation.clock: Elapsed seconds from contact, separate from all dated catalogue clocks. The scrubber follows the authored viewing pace so sub-second encounter motion is accessible alongside the five-hour interval. Its value text reports physical elapsed time.
presentation.guidedPace: 66 authored seconds: -30s to -2s over 4s; to -0.2s over 3s; to contact over 5s; contact hold 0.5s; to +5s over 6.5s; to +60s over 10s; to +10min over 10s; to half an original orbit over 9s; to three original periods over 18s. Stops at the bound.
presentation.camera: Close on two illustrative bodies, hold the last 10 km camera distance for visible convergence; push into cloud A and follow its actual centroid for ten model minutes; continuously pull back to Earth from +10 to +40 minutes. Follow cloud retains the close camera; Frame Earth reveals the whole scene. Floating origin preserves local precision; positions are not exaggerated.
presentation.glyphs: Two authored 3D body diagrams before contact; 768 irregular shaded shard glyphs after contact. Display sizes, rotation and body shapes are authored, not material-fracture outputs. Contact ring is a marker, not a fireball. 24 short model histories in the frame translating with the family mean release orbit reveal dispersion within cloud A; tips meet exact current fragment positions. Original orbit paths default off. Scale bar reports target-plane distance.
presentation.slider: Pauses at the displayed time; changes the maximum paired kick magnitude while holding seed, directions and relative magnitudes fixed; directly recomputes physical states and periods.
presentation.reducedMotion: Opening and replay stay paused. Later preference changes pause and never automatically restart.
presentation.navigation: Discover and cross-links distinguish the synthetic experiment from the retained catalogue chapter.

references.role: Primary reference for the two-body initial-state problem and elliptic Kepler equation; no SPICE code copied or runtime dependency.
Primary reference for Earth GM, reference radius and nominal rotation rate. Numerical constants only.

rights.model: Edition-owned MIT code and synthetic initial conditions; no satellite records or licensed breakup dataset acquired.
rights.geography: Existing audited Natural Earth public-domain geometry is unchanged.

validation.unit: Encounter geometry, circular closure, seeded replay, paired variable-speed kicks filling velocity space, momentum and kinetic energy at slider extrema, positive perigees, orbital energy/angular momentum on forward/reverse seeks. Independent Cartesian RK4 with 2-second steps agrees after three orbits within 0.1 m position and 1 mm/s velocity. Camera checks cover real-centroid following, contact and pullback continuity, and aspect adaptation.
validation.browser: Guided hold/release/stop, seek/replay/spread, camera clock preservation, reduced motion, keyboard, model scrolling, portrait/landscape, /zenit/ assets, no external requests. Actual bright-shard raster footprint spans a filled area in the young cloud; cloud follow is independent of the orbital reveal and preserves time.
validation.interpretation: Numerical validation of this authored two-body experiment, not empirical validation of fragmentation physics or a historical event.
